description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between translation quality, measured by BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy), and latency, measured by Average Lagging (AL), in a Wait-k Policy for machine translation. The x-axis represents the Average Lagging (AL) with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 6, and the y-axis represents the BLEU score with a linear scale ranging from 12 to 28. There are four lines representing different consistency settings: Consistency-CE (dashed purple line with circle markers), Inconsistency-CE (solid purple line with square markers), Inconsistency-CE-MP (dashed blue line with square markers), and Consistency-Bi (solid red line with star markers). The Consistency-CE line starts at a BLEU score of approximately 14 and ends at around 26, showing a steady increase. The Inconsistency-CE line begins at a BLEU score of about 16 and ends at approximately 24, also showing a steady increase. The Inconsistency-CE-MP line starts at a BLEU score of around 18 and ends at about 26, with a slight dip in the middle before continuing to rise. The Consistency-Bi line begins at a BLEU score of approximately 22 and ends at around 28, with a consistent upward trend. The plot does not provide specific data points for the start and end of the x-axis, but the trends suggest that as latency increases, the translation quality also tends to improve, with the Consistency-Bi setting achieving the highest BLEU score at the highest latency.
